terms.gloss: a school, especially of rhetoric or philosophy; a lecture
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.102: quī cum in scholā assēdissent (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek σχολή, leisure, and so leisure given to learning: a lecture, then the place where one is given (Lewis & Short). lūdus is the children’s school; schola the school of a rhetor or philosopher, and the school of Comenius and the colloquia.

evidence: M-O s.v. school types: high school (schola secundāria)
terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase. Morgan–Owens’s schola secundāria is also in use, but classically secundārius is second-rate, of bread and honey (Col., Plin., Suet.; Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Praeceptor sedet in cathedrā; discipulī in subselliīs; ille docet, hī discunt.
phrases.english: The teacher sits in the chair, the pupils on the benches; he teaches, they learn.
